title: Transfer of bilinear sheaf pairings along ringed precomposition
statement: Let $(C,J),(D,K)$ be sites small relative to a fixed coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $v:C\to D$ be a functor such that precomposition sends sheaves on $D$ to sheaves on $C$, let $R,S$ be commutative ring sheaves on $C,D$, and let $c:R\to v_*S$ be a unital ring-sheaf map. For an $S$-module sheaf $M$, set $(PM)(U)=M(vU)$ with $R(U)$ acting through $c_U$, and let $P$ act on morphisms by precomposition [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For any $S$-module sheaves $M,N,T$, let $b:M\times N\to T$ be a morphism of underlying sheaves of sets which is $S(V)$-bilinear for every $V\in D$. There is a unique $R$-module-sheaf morphism $\overline b:PM\otimes_RPN\to PT$ such that $\overline b_U(x\otimes y)=b_{vU}(x,y)$ for all $U\in C$, $x\in M(vU)$ and $y\in N(vU)$, where the source pure tensor is its canonical image in the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For another such pairing $b':M'\times N'\to T'$ and $S$-linear sheaf maps $f:M\to M'$, $g:N\to N'$, $h:T\to T'$ with $h_V(b_V(x,y))=b'_V(f_Vx,g_Vy)$ for every $V,x,y$, the induced morphisms satisfy $P(h)\circ\overline b=\overline{b'}\circ(Pf\otimes_RPg)$.

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward) and 03EK (section-tensor-product, Hom/Bilin display); agent extraction of transfer and naturality.

proof.text: For an $S$-module sheaf $A$ define $r\cdot a=c_U(r)a$ on $(PA)(U)=A(vU)$. The additive and multiplicative identities and $c_U(1)=1$ give the module axioms. For $t:U'\to U$, naturality of $c$ and semilinearity of restrictions give $(c_U(r)a)|_{vU'}=c_{U'}(r|_{U'})(a|_{vU'})$. Its underlying presheaf is a sheaf by the precomposition hypothesis. Thus $PA$ is an $R$-module sheaf by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If $k:A\to B$ is $S$-linear, then $k_{vU}(c_U(r)a)=c_U(r)k_{vU}(a)$, so precomposition gives an $R$-linear sheaf map $Pk$. Identities and compositions hold componentwise, making $P$ a functor.

source.place: Tag 03D6 (definition-pushforward), restriction of scalars; the verification for precomposition is written out.

proof.text: Put $\beta_U(x,y)=b_{vU}(x,y)$. Additivity in both variables is inherited from $b_{vU}$. For $r\in R(U)$, $\beta_U(r\cdot x,y)=b_{vU}(c_U(r)x,y)=c_U(r)b_{vU}(x,y)=r\cdot\beta_U(x,y)$, and $\beta_U(x,r\cdot y)=r\cdot\beta_U(x,y)$ by the same $S(vU)$-bilinearity in the second variable. For $t:U'\to U$, naturality of $b$ says $\beta_U(x,y)|_{vU'}=\beta_{U'}(x|_{vU'},y|_{vU'})$. Hence $\beta:PM\times PN\to PT$ is a morphism of sheaves of sets, sectionwise $R$-bilinear with the module structures of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tags 03D6 (definition-pushforward) and 03EK (section-tensor-product), definition of Bilin; scalar and restriction computations.

proof.text: For the restricted bilinear family of step 2, apply TensorProduct.lift sectionwise. Compatibility with restrictions, checked by tensor induction, assembles these maps into a morphism of presheaves from PM.val tensor PN.val to PT.val [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product]. The sheafification adjunction [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] factors this morphism through the sheafification. Precompose with tensorObjIsoSheafification.hom [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] to obtain the required sheaf tensor morphism. The unit equation of the adjunction proves its pure-tensor formula. For uniqueness, precompose two proposed maps with tensorObjIsoSheafification.inv and use injectivity of the adjunction correspondence; tensor induction proves equality of the presheaf morphisms. This is the existing bilinear-universal-property argument generalized privately to independent site and coefficient universes, since its public declaration equates those universes.

Naturality of the counit of module sheafification and the tensorator of its monoidal functor proves naturality of tensorObjIsoSheafification in both factors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Combine this with naturality of the sheafification unit [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Evaluation on x tensor y then says that the tensor of Pf and Pg sends the canonical pure tensor of x,y to that of f(x),g(y) [def-pur-presheaf-tensor-product]. Apply the uniqueness argument of step 3 to the R-bilinear pairing (x,y) mapping to h(b(x,y)). The left composite has this formula by the formula for the constructed map; the right composite has it by the tensor-map formula, the assumed formula for the other transfer, and compatibility of f,g,h with b,b'. Thus the two composites are equal without any global generation assumption.
